competitive_landscape: Today: long 4WD road transfers, charter air and occasional private boats. The pain is slow, dusty, high-friction guest journeys at a destination selling seclusion — exactly the status quo a silent foiling tier improves on.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: All on-island legs — Tambolaka↔NIHI (~35 nm), ↔Waikabubak, ↔Kodi/Pero — sit inside the all-electric envelope with resort-microgrid charging at NIHI and Cap Karoso.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Carries the cross-island east arm (~120 nm) and the hero-chain legs to Komodo (~140 nm) and Bali (~210 nm) with no charging dependence at greenfield jetties.

precedents.what: A foiling-electric vessel network at national scale (~100 vessels / $100M, 3-year phasing)
precedents.why_it_matters: Proves foiling-electric works as an at-scale transfer-and-island-hopping network — the model the Bali→Lombok→Komodo→Sumba chain extends.

regulatory_note: Indonesian transport-side certification (Kemenhub/DGST + BKI) plus Sumbanese customary/Marapu protocol as the primary local gate; no UNESCO conservation overlay on Sumba itself (distinct from Komodo NP).
seasonality: SE dry monsoon (May–Oct) is the peak season with calm water; NW wet monsoon (Dec–Mar) is more variable, with cyclone-edge risk Feb–Mar (NTT is cyclone-exposed). Best window Jun–Sep.
summary: Sumba is one of the world's most rarefied low-density luxury islands, anchored by NIHI Sumba (repeatedly ranked the world's best hotel) and Cap Karoso. It is the terminus of the Bali → Lombok → Komodo → Sumba luxury island-hopping chain. Guest journeys today are long 4WD road transfers from the Tambolaka airport gateway to the SW resort coast; a foiling-electric transfer layer collapses that friction and completes the chain as a genuinely sea-linked journey.
tagline: The terminus of the island-hopping chain — jet-to-foil-to-villa.
